title: Boundary, Environment, Context and Dependency
results: Boundary is dimension-specific and there is no universal Runtime perimeter.
Isolation is a vector over namespace, authority, resource, failure, information and other dimensions rather than a boolean.
Process, namespace, authority, resource and provider boundaries are distinct.
Path/object resolution is namespace/context dependent; same textual path does not prove same resolved object.
Current P4 proves Runtime-host-namespace path witness does not establish target namespace integrity or byte consumption.
Execution Environment, observer State and broader Context are distinct roles/projections.
Explicit inputs are only a subset of possible dependencies.
Dependency is claim-relative and can be direct, transitive, ambient, authority, kernel/hardware, network/service or temporal/random.
Dependency handling must distinguish freeze, materialize, bind, witness, virtualize, query/reconcile and leave-open.
Dynamic linking and current P2/P3 prove executable digest is not execution-closure digest and arbitrary static complete closure is unavailable.
Immutable inputs provide strong Runtime-owned byte/materialization closure only for declared explicit inputs.
Host Dependencies are declared filesystem prerequisites plus a Runtime-host-namespace continuity witness, not automatic discovery or target-view immutability.
ExecutionProviderSnapshot closes Runtime-owned dispatch-provider identity only.
Fixed process environment/locale reduces ambient variability but does not close kernel, time, randomness, device or network dependencies.
Containers compose host-kernel boundaries; VMs add guest-kernel boundaries; neither creates a closed universe.
Hermeticity, determinism, isolation and reproducibility are distinct properties.
Dependency closure is relative to the claim and may be impossible to enumerate for arbitrary open-world execution.
Authority restriction can reduce dependency surface and sometimes engineer closure more strongly than dependency enumeration.
Stronger isolation can alter target semantics and therefore is not automatically transparent or superior.
Current Ordivon should continue strong narrow closure claims with explicit open-world disclaimers rather than inventing a fully captured environment abstraction.

nextRound.title: Resource, Capacity, Constraint and Scarcity
nextRound.entryQuestion: Which things enable or constrain realization as resources, how do capacity/availability/allocation/reservation differ, and what does scarcity or pressure mean for Runtime?

notes: RF7 explains boundary/environment/dependency closure but does not authorize container/VM adoption, automatic dependency discovery, network capture, new namespace isolation or Host Dependency changes.
